# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1463
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1463
- **Title**: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1459` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1669
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:53:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:58:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN: `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — settle mid-drain → notice steered → reaction run executes → exit 0 after the result landed (reproduces the gh-1440 shape); error settle → error steer; suppressed job → no reaction run; never-settling job → ceiling → detach summary; `shellJobDrainMs: 0` kill switch.
- Pure UT: `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` (config parse + drain decision).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: pending — rerunning with full logs to identify the single failure seen in the first pass (all config/parity/cli targeted suites green).

### Notes

- The drain wake legs ride Dart's monotonic timer clock while the ceiling deadline reads the wall clock, so the 10-round cap can exhaust a few ms before the wall deadline is observed — the post-loop still-active check makes that exit print the same ceiling line (no silent path).
- With `--wait-for-jobs`, the drain ceiling bounds the reaction-run phase; the flag's own `waiting.waitCeilingMinutes` still governs the final wait for never-settling waiters.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1463._

> ℹ️ **19 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

---

### Thread 22

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: Solid fix for gh-1459 — the headless drain now covers background shell jobs with a shared wall-clock ceiling, and the ask-4 interim liveness steers (probe-generation suppression included) match the ticket spec. Verified locally: `dart analyze` clean on the touched lifecycle/config files, and 245 targeted tests green (drain ITs, liveness ITs, config UTs, stuck-tool, cli_config, bash_job resolution, shell_jobs, parity suites). Ticket asks #1–#4 are all covered; the earlier-red `stuck_tool_session_test` was adapted correctly to the new drain contract.

2. (suggestion) `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain, not just shell jobs — see inline comment on `headless_config.dart`.
3. Two cosmetic wording/consistency nits (detach-line attribution, negative-elapsed clamp) — see inline comments.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1463
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1463
- **Title**: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1459` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1669
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:53:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:58:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN: `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — settle mid-drain → notice steered → reaction run executes → exit 0 after the result landed (reproduces the gh-1440 shape); error settle → error steer; suppressed job → no reaction run; never-settling job → ceiling → detach summary; `shellJobDrainMs: 0` kill switch.
- Pure UT: `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` (config parse + drain decision).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: pending — rerunning with full logs to identify the single failure seen in the first pass (all config/parity/cli targeted suites green).

### Notes

- The drain wake legs ride Dart's monotonic timer clock while the ceiling deadline reads the wall clock, so the 10-round cap can exhaust a few ms before the wall deadline is observed — the post-loop still-active check makes that exit print the same ceiling line (no silent path).
- With `--wait-for-jobs`, the drain ceiling bounds the reaction-run phase; the flag's own `waiting.waitCeilingMinutes` still governs the final wait for never-settling waiters.

# pr-1463: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)

## Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN: `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — settle mid-drain → notice steered → reaction run executes → exit 0 after the result landed (reproduces the gh-1440 shape); error settle → error steer; suppressed job → no reaction run; never-settling job → ceiling → detach summary; `shellJobDrainMs: 0` kill switch.
- Pure UT: `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` (config parse + drain decision).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: pending — rerunning with full logs to identify the single failure seen in the first pass (all config/parity/cli targeted suites green).

### Notes

- The drain wake legs ride Dart's monotonic timer clock while the ceiling deadline reads the wall clock, so the 10-round cap can exhaust a few ms before the wall deadline is observed — the post-loop still-active check makes that exit print the same ceiling line (no silent path).
- With `--wait-for-jobs`, the drain ceiling bounds the reaction-run phase; the flag's own `waiting.waitCeilingMinutes` still governs the final wait for never-settling waiters.

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1463
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1463
- **Title**: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1459` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1669
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:53:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:58:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN: `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — settle mid-drain → notice steered → reaction run executes → exit 0 after the result landed (reproduces the gh-1440 shape); error settle → error steer; suppressed job → no reaction run; never-settling job → ceiling → detach summary; `shellJobDrainMs: 0` kill switch.
- Pure UT: `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` (config parse + drain decision).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: pending — rerunning with full logs to identify the single failure seen in the first pass (all config/parity/cli targeted suites green).

### Notes

- The drain wake legs ride Dart's monotonic timer clock while the ceiling deadline reads the wall clock, so the 10-round cap can exhaust a few ms before the wall deadline is observed — the post-loop still-active check makes that exit print the same ceiling line (no silent path).
- With `--wait-for-jobs`, the drain ceiling bounds the reaction-run phase; the flag's own `waiting.waitCeilingMinutes` still governs the final wait for never-settling waiters.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1463._

> ℹ️ **19 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

---

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1463
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1463
- **Title**: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1459` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1669
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:53:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:58:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN: `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — settle mid-drain → notice steered → reaction run executes → exit 0 after the result landed (reproduces the gh-1440 shape); error settle → error steer; suppressed job → no reaction run; never-settling job → ceiling → detach summary; `shellJobDrainMs: 0` kill switch.
- Pure UT: `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` (config parse + drain decision).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: pending — rerunning with full logs to identify the single failure seen in the first pass (all config/parity/cli targeted suites green).

### Notes

- The drain wake legs ride Dart's monotonic timer clock while the ceiling deadline reads the wall clock, so the 10-round cap can exhaust a few ms before the wall deadline is observed — the post-loop still-active check makes that exit print the same ceiling line (no silent path).
- With `--wait-for-jobs`, the drain ceiling bounds the reaction-run phase; the flag's own `waiting.waitCeilingMinutes` still governs the final wait for never-settling waiters.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1463
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1463
- **Title**: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1459` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 16
- **Additions**: +1669
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:53:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T12:58:52Z

## PR Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

- RED→GREEN: `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — settle mid-drain → notice steered → reaction run executes → exit 0 after the result landed (reproduces the gh-1440 shape); error settle → error steer; suppressed job → no reaction run; never-settling job → ceiling → detach summary; `shellJobDrainMs: 0` kill switch.
- Pure UT: `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` (config parse + drain decision).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: pending — rerunning with full logs to identify the single failure seen in the first pass (all config/parity/cli targeted suites green).

### Notes

- The drain wake legs ride Dart's monotonic timer clock while the ceiling deadline reads the wall clock, so the 10-round cap can exhaust a few ms before the wall deadline is observed — the post-loop still-active check makes that exit print the same ceiling line (no silent path).
- With `--wait-for-jobs`, the drain ceiling bounds the reaction-run phase; the flag's own `waiting.waitCeilingMinutes` still governs the final wait for never-settling waiters.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1463._

> ℹ️ **19 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# pr-1463: gh-1459 [BUG] Headless exits with live background shell jobs (detached, results lost) — must drain+steer like subagents (gh-1440 run orphaned its full-suite job)

## Description

Closes #1459
### Root Cause

`_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`) drained only in-flight **subagent** jobs before headless exit; background **shell jobs** (`bash background:true`, `ShellJobRegistry`) were never consulted. Headless fell straight through to the detach summary (`waitingDetachSummary`, issue #450 AC7) and exited — killing any live job with the process, so the model never saw results it was explicitly waiting for (the gh-1440 run orphaned its full `dart test` suite and never wrote `outputs/response.md`).

### Fix

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` (new): `headless:` config section with `shellJobDrainMs` — the wall-clock ceiling for the headless background-job drain (default 30 min, `0` = pre-fix behavior) — plus the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` drain decision (active → drain; none → exit; ceiling spent → detach).
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`: `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` now drains live shell jobs exactly like subagents — waits the settles (the existing `_onShellJobSettled` fresh-turn-while-idle path steers each result into a reaction run), awaits the reaction run, loops (10-round cap), under ONE shared ceiling for both loops. Suppressed jobs (`suppressSettleNotification` — result already landed in-turn) are not awaited; a settle landing outside a round still gets its reaction run awaited; anything outliving the ceiling prints an observable `⏳ … drain ceiling … — detaching` line, then today's detach summary applies (never a silent hang). A `⏳ waiting: …` line (#1055 parity) names what the run stays alive for.
- Config wiring: `cli_config.dart` (strict `headless:` yaml parse + save-when-non-default), `agent_cli_config.dart`, `bin/fah_runapp.dart`, parity registry (`fileOnlyConfigKeys['headless']`).
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) unchanged.

### Test Coverage

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1463._
