## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1463._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: A late drain wake consumes every crossed quiet bucket with a single steer**

Here a due steer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot:

```dart
liveness.consumedBucket[job.id] = elapsedMs ~/ liveness.quietMs;
```

This is exact on cadence (the tested path — the wake is pulled to the next threshold, so normally exactly one bucket is new). But if the drain wakes late with several thresholds crossed — e.g. a reaction run triggered by a settle or a previous steer outlives two `shellJobQuietMs` windows — ONE notice is steered and buckets 2..N are all consumed silently. The ticket's budget edge case states "N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices (test counts), never per-timer duplicates", which this path doesn't honor.

Options: steer one notice *per* newly-crossed bucket in a loop here, or consciously document that a burst after a long reaction run collapses to a single notice (arguably the right UX — the model wasn't blind, it was busy). Either is fine; worth a comment either way since the current code reads as if the ticket's invariant holds unconditionally.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disables the pre-existing subagent drain**

With `drainMs: 0` the deadline equals `now`, so the very first `_headlessDrainAction` returns `detach` for *any* active job — including in-flight subagent (`TaskJob`) jobs. But the subagent drain loop existed before gh-1459 and was uncapped: pre-PR, headless always waited for in-flight subagents regardless of any config. So the `0` kill switch — documented as "the pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately behavior" — actually detaches *more* than gh-1459's predecessor did for subagent-only waits, and a knob named `shellJobDrainMs` reads as shell-job-scoped while it gates both loops.

Consider either gating only the shell-job leg on `0` (keeping the legacy subagent drain unconditional), or adjusting the doc comment on `HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs` / the AGENTS.md bullet to state explicitly that `0` disables the whole drain including subagents. The shared ceiling for both loops under the default 30 min is per ticket and fine — this is only about the `0` edge.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: The detach line attributes the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain**

This message prints whenever jobs are still active after the loop, but the loop can also end because the 10-round cap exhausted while the wall-clock ceiling still had budget (the PR notes acknowledge the race). In that case the line says `drain ceiling (1800000 ms) reached`, which misattributes the cause and could send someone tuning `shellJobDrainMs` when the real lever is job settle latency vs. the round cap.

Minor wording fix, e.g. naming both possible causes — `drain ceiling (N ms) or round cap reached — detaching` — or threading a flag from the loop exit reason. Behavior is correct either way; this is debuggability only.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Clamp the elapsed Duration before it reaches the notice text**

The bucket math correctly guards a negative elapsed (`elapsed.isNegative ? 0 : …`), but `headlessLivenessElapsedText(elapsed)` a few lines below receives the *unclamped* `Duration`. When the waiting clock sits behind `job.startedAt` — possible under the fake-clock seam used by the drain ITs, since `ShellJobEntry.startedAt` is hard-wired to real `DateTime.now()` — `inMinutes`/`inSeconds` truncate toward zero and the notice can render a negative clause like `-3s elapsed`.

Production (both real wall clocks) can never hit this, so it's cosmetic; passing the clamped duration through (e.g. building the text from `Duration(milliseconds: elapsedMs)`) keeps the two calculations consistent and test-seam-proof for one line.

---

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately), then the detach summary applies

  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Wait — check the burst timing math. Fake clock starts at real now (t0 ≈ startedAt). 

- Round 1 sleep: clock t0 → request adds d1 = 5m (due = startedAt+5m, now≈t0 → d≈5m). Clock = t0+5m. Release → steer: elapsed = 5m → bucket 1 → notice '5m'. consumed=1.
- Test advances +10m → clock = t0+15m.
- Round 2: wakeIn: bucket = consumed+1 = 2 → due = startedAt + 10m = t0+10m → d = due - now = -5m! Negative duration sleep. Hmm — `wakeIn` computes `d = due.difference(now); if (d < wake) wake = d;` → wake = -5m (negative). `_waitingSleep(-5m)` → clock = clock + (-5m) = t0+10m. Gate parked. 

Uh oh: the clock goes BACKWARD (t0+15m → t0+10m) at sleep request. Then release → steer: elapsed = 10m → bucket 2 → crossed {2} only → ONE notice '10m'. Then round 3: due = t0+15m, now t0+10m → d=5m → clock t0+15m → steer '15m'. So the burst as written yields sequential notices 10m, 15m, 20m... in separate rounds — NOT a burst, and my expected count of 3 after the second release is wrong (only 1 more at that point; total waits would time out expecting 3).

I need the advanceClockBy to happen BEFORE round 2's sleep is REQUESTED, so the sleep request itself computes d from the advanced clock. Sequence: after release #1 and notice #1 steered, the drain loops immediately and requests round-2 sleep right away (before I can advance the clock in between — race).

Better approach: make the LATE wake land by advancing the clock while the sleep gate is parked, but ensure the requested duration was computed from the pre-advance clock and the released steer sees the advanced clock. That was my original design — the problem is `waitingSleep` advances the clock by the REQUESTED d at request time. So at request time clock moves to t0+10m already (d=5m from t0+5m). Wait, recompute: after round 1, clock = t0+5m. Round 2 sleep request: due = startedAt + quiet*2 = t0+10m; d = 5m; clock = t0+10m at REQUEST. Gate parked. Test advances +10m → t0+20m. Release → steer: elapsed = 20m → bucket 4 → crossed {2,3,4} → 3 notices ('10m','15m','20m'). Total livenessRuns = 4. My test then expects livenessRuns == 3 after the burst... wrong: 1 + 3 = 4. Then the "resumed cadence" part: consumed = 4; round 3 sleep: due = t0+25m, clock t0+20m → d=5m → clock t0+25m → release → steer '25m' (5th notice). But I only added 4 liveness scripts; the 5th notice run would get default 'noted.' — fine (router falls back).

So simplify: drop the "resumed cadence" section and assert: after burst release, livenessRuns == 4, notices 2..4 are '10m','15m','20m elapsed'. Then finish the job; assert final count 4.

But wait — burst steering 3 notices: each notice steered via `_startRun`/`_agent.steer`. The FIRST starts a fresh run; the second and third: after first `_startRun(message)`, isBusy becomes true → subsequent steers ride `_agent.steer`. All three payloads recorded as separate contexts with _livenessMarker. The router pops livenessScripts 3 times. Good.

One more check on ordering: the steer loop awaits `_shellJobs.tail(job.id)` once before the loop (async). Fine.

Also — the third notice in the same burst: elapsed text '20m elapsed'. `Duration(milliseconds: 4 * 3000)` → 20m → '20m'. Good.

  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately), then the detach summary applies

  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE

  the bash_job escape hatch), skipped for a crossing the model probed

blocks.text:
Wait — check the burst timing math. Fake clock starts at real now (t0 ≈ startedAt). 

- Round 1 sleep: clock t0 → request adds d1 = 5m (due = startedAt+5m, now≈t0 → d≈5m). Clock = t0+5m. Release → steer: elapsed = 5m → bucket 1 → notice '5m'. consumed=1.
- Test advances +10m → clock = t0+15m.
- Round 2: wakeIn: bucket = consumed+1 = 2 → due = startedAt + 10m = t0+10m → d = due - now = -5m! Negative duration sleep. Hmm — `wakeIn` computes `d = due.difference(now); if (d < wake) wake = d;` → wake = -5m (negative). `_waitingSleep(-5m)` → clock = clock + (-5m) = t0+10m. Gate parked. 

Uh oh: the clock goes BACKWARD (t0+15m → t0+10m) at sleep request. Then release → steer: elapsed = 10m → bucket 2 → crossed {2} only → ONE notice '10m'. Then round 3: due = t0+15m, now t0+10m → d=5m → clock t0+15m → steer '15m'. So the burst as written yields sequential notices 10m, 15m, 20m... in separate rounds — NOT a burst, and my expected count of 3 after the second release is wrong (only 1 more at that point; total waits would time out expecting 3).

I need the advanceClockBy to happen BEFORE round 2's sleep is REQUESTED, so the sleep request itself computes d from the advanced clock. Sequence: after release #1 and notice #1 steered, the drain loops immediately and requests round-2 sleep right away (before I can advance the clock in between — race).

Better approach: make the LATE wake land by advancing the clock while the sleep gate is parked, but ensure the requested duration was computed from the pre-advance clock and the released steer sees the advanced clock. (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Headless `fa -p` DRAINS live shell
  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately), then the detach summary applies
  (gh-1459). While the drain waits, every `headless.shellJobQuietMs`
  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE

  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Headless `fa -p` DRAINS live shell
  jobs after the final answer like in-flight subagents — the settles
  steer fresh reaction turns, loop (10 rounds) under ONE shared
  wall-clock ceiling `headless.shellJobDrainMs` (default 30 min; 0 =
  pre-gh-1459 detach-immediately), then the detach summary applies
  (gh-1459). While the drain waits, every `headless.shellJobQuietMs`
  (default 5 min; 0 = off) of a still-running awaited job steers ONE
  interim liveness notice (`job <id> running · <elapsed> · tail: …` +
  the bash_job escape hatch), skipped for a crossing the model probed
  itself (`bash_job status/output` bumps the entry's probe generation)
  (gh-1459 ask #4). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.

Then round 3: due = t0+15m, now t0+10m → d=5m → clock t0+15m → steer '15m'. Wait — check the burst timing math. Fake clock starts at real now (t0 ≈ startedAt). 

- Round 1 sleep: clock t0 → request adds d1 = 5m (due = startedAt+5m, now≈t0 → d≈5m). Clock = t0+5m. Release → steer: elapsed = 5m → bucket 1 → notice '5m'. consumed=1.
- Test advances +10m → clock = t0+15m.
- Round 2: wakeIn: bucket = consumed+1 = 2 → due = startedAt + 10m = t0+10m → d = due - now = -5m! Negative duration sleep. Hmm — `wakeIn` computes `d = due.difference(now); if (d < wake) wake = d;` → wake = -5m (negative). `_waitingSleep(-5m)` → clock = clock + (-5m) = t0+10m. Gate parked. 

Uh oh: the clock goes BACKWARD (t0+15m → t0+10m) at sleep request. Then release → steer: elapsed = 10m → bucket 2 → crossed {2} only → ONE notice '10m'. Then round 3: due = t0+15m, now t0+10m → d=5m → clock t0+15m → steer '15m'. So the burst as written yields sequential notices 10m, 15m, 20m... in separate rounds — NOT a burst, and my expected count of 3 after the second release is wrong (only 1 more at that point; total waits would time out expecting 3).

I need the advanceClockBy to happen BEFORE round 2's sleep is REQUESTED, so the sleep request itself computes d from the advanced clock. Sequence: after release #1 and notice #1 steered, the drain loops immediately and requests round-2 sleep right away (before I can advance the clock in between — race).

Better approach: make the LATE wake land by advancing the clock while the sleep gate is parked, but ensure the requested duration was computed from the pre-advance clock and the released steer sees the advanced clock. That was my original design — the problem is `waitingSleep` advances the clock by the REQUESTED d at request time. So at request time clock moves to t0+10m already (d=5m from t0+5m). Wait, recompute: after round 1, clock = t0+5m. Round 2 sleep request: due = startedAt + quiet*2 = t0+10m; d = 5m; clock = t0+10m at REQUEST. Gate parked. Test advances +10m → t0+20m. Then the "resumed cadence" part: consumed = 4; round 3 sleep: due = t0+25m, clock t0+20m → d=5m → clock t0+25m → release → steer '25m' (5th notice). If the run ends after the first answer while more steered messages are queued, another fresh run starts for notice 3, etc. Either way each notice yields a context whose last user text contains the marker and is not a tool continuation. The count should be 4. There may be timing subtleties but the waitFor loop handles async.

## Fixed — one notice per newly-crossed bucket

Implemented the per-bucket option so the ticket's invariant ("N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices") now holds unconditionally, including on a late wake.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` — `_steerHeadlessLiveness`:** a due steer no longer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot. ## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

**`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction`:** the pure decision now takes `hasActiveSubAgents` / `hasActiveShellJobs` (replacing the combined `hasActiveJobs`) plus `shellDrainDisabled`. With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. The round honors the legacy shape: with the switch on and subagents active it awaits the settles directly (`Future.wait`) instead of racing a zero-length ceiling sleep — without that, the zero deadline would have woken every round instantly and burned the 10-round cap in microseconds, detaching anyway. Doc comments updated (`HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs`, the lifecycle method, and the AGENTS.md bullet) to state the shell-scoped semantics explicitly.

**RED → GREEN:**
- Pure UTs in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`: `shellDrainDisabled` with only subagents → `drain` (even with the ceiling spent), with shell jobs → `detach` immediately, with neither → `exit`; the existing shared-ceiling cases now pin that a spent ceiling detaches subagents too when the knob is non-zero.
- New IT `shellJobDrainMs: 0 keeps the legacy subagent drain — an in-flight subagent still drains before exit` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — a background `task` child that settles at 800 ms must still re-enter as a `<task-result` wake run before exit with `drainMs: 0`. Pre-fix the run detached immediately and the result was lost; now it drains and exits 0 with no detach line. The existing shell-job `0` kill-switch IT still passes (shell jobs detach at once).

{"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

**`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction`:** the pure decision now takes `hasActiveSubAgents` / `hasActiveShellJobs` (replacing the combined `hasActiveJobs`) plus `shellDrainDisabled`. With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. The round honors the legacy shape: with the switch on and subagents active it awaits the settles directly (`Future.wait`) instead of racing a zero-length ceiling sleep — without that, the zero deadline would have woken every round instantly and burned the 10-round cap in microseconds, detaching anyway. Doc comments updated (`HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs`, the lifecycle method, and the AGENTS.md bullet) to state the shell-scoped semantics explicitly.

- Pure UTs in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`: `shellDrainDisabled` with only subagents → `drain` (even with the ceiling spent), with shell jobs → `detach` immediately, with neither → `exit`; the existing shared-ceiling cases now pin that a spent ceiling detaches subagents too when the knob is non-zero.

{"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

**`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction`:** the pure decision now takes `hasActiveSubAgents` / `hasActiveShellJobs` (replacing the combined `hasActiveJobs`) plus `shellDrainDisabled`. With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. The round honors the legacy shape: with the switch on and subagents active it awaits the settles directly (`Future.wait`) instead of racing a zero-length ceiling sleep — without that, the zero deadline would have woken every round instantly and burned the 10-round cap in microseconds, detaching anyway. Doc comments updated (`HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs`, the lifecycle method, and the AGENTS.md bullet) to state the shell-scoped semantics explicitly.

**RED → GREEN:**
- Pure UTs in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`: `shellDrainDisabled` with only subagents → `drain` (even with the ceiling spent), with shell jobs → `detach` immediately, with neither → `exit`; the existing shared-ceiling cases now pin that a spent ceiling detaches subagents too when the knob is non-zero.
- New IT `shellJobDrainMs: 0 keeps the legacy subagent drain — an in-flight subagent still drains before exit` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — a background `task` child that settles at 800 ms must still re-enter as a `<task-result` wake run before exit with `drainMs: 0`. {"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

{"content":"## Fixed — one notice per newly-crossed bucket

Implemented the per-bucket option so the ticket's invariant ("N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices") now holds unconditionally, including on a late wake.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` — `_steerHeadlessLiveness`:** a due steer no longer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot. The code computes `currentBucket` vs `lastConsumedBucket` and, when a long reaction run left several thresholds crossed at once, steers **one notice per newly-crossed bucket** (`for (var bucket = lastBucket + 1; bucket <= currentBucket; bucket++)`), each stamped from its *own* threshold via the extracted `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice(job, noticeElapsed: Duration(milliseconds: bucket * quietMs), tail: tail)` — so a burst after a 10-minute reaction run renders `5m`, `10m`, `15m` … rather than one collapsed notice. Probe semantics are unchanged in spirit: a `bash_job status/output` probe since the last consumption suppresses the whole burst (it was watching, not blind) but still consumes every crossed bucket — no replay on the next wake. The behavior is documented in the code comment at the consumption point, as suggested.

**RED → GREEN:** new fake-clock IT `a late drain wake (a long reaction run) steers ONE notice PER newly-crossed quiet bucket` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_liveness_test.dart` — the harness gained `advanceClockBy` to simulate a wake landing ~15m out with buckets 1–3 un-consumed; it asserts exactly 3 notice user-messages (`5m`/`10m`/`15m elapsed`) in the transcript. It failed pre-fix (1 collapsed notice) and passes now; the two pre-existing cadence/probe ITs stay green (normal wakes still land exactly one bucket at a time, so no behavior change on the tested path).

{"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

**`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction`:** the pure decision now takes `hasActiveSubAgents` / `hasActiveShellJobs` (replacing the combined `hasActiveJobs`) plus `shellDrainDisabled`. With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. The round honors the legacy shape: with the switch on and subagents active it awaits the settles directly (`Future.wait`) instead of racing a zero-length ceiling sleep — without that, the zero deadline would have woken every round instantly and burned the 10-round cap in microseconds, detaching anyway. Doc comments updated (`HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs`, the lifecycle method, and the AGENTS.md bullet) to state the shell-scoped semantics explicitly.

**RED → GREEN:**
- Pure UTs in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`: `shellDrainDisabled` with only subagents → `drain` (even with the ceiling spent), with shell jobs → `detach` immediately, with neither → `exit`; the existing shared-ceiling cases now pin that a spent ceiling detaches subagents too when the knob is non-zero.
- New IT `shellJobDrainMs: 0 keeps the legacy subagent drain — an in-flight subagent still drains before exit` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — a background `task` child that settles at 800 ms must still re-enter as a `<task-result` wake run before exit with `drainMs: 0`. Pre-fix the run detached immediately and the result was lost; now it drains and exits 0 with no detach line. The existing shell-job `0` kill-switch IT still passes (shell jobs detach at once).

{"content":"## Fixed — one notice per newly-crossed bucket

Implemented the per-bucket option so the ticket's invariant ("N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices") now holds unconditionally, including on a late wake.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` — `_steerHeadlessLiveness`:** a due steer no longer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot. The code computes `currentBucket` vs `lastConsumedBucket` and, when a long reaction run left several thresholds crossed at once, steers **one notice per newly-crossed bucket** (`for (var bucket = lastBucket + 1; bucket <= currentBucket; bucket++)`), each stamped from its *own* threshold via the extracted `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice(job, noticeElapsed: Duration(milliseconds: bucket * quietMs), tail: tail)` — so a burst after a 10-minute reaction run renders `5m`, `10m`, `15m` … rather than one collapsed notice. Probe semantics are unchanged in spirit: a `bash_job status/output` probe since the last consumption suppresses the whole burst (it was watching, not blind) but still consumes every crossed bucket — no replay on the next wake. {"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

**`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction`:** the pure decision now takes `hasActiveSubAgents` / `hasActiveShellJobs` (replacing the combined `hasActiveJobs`) plus `shellDrainDisabled`. With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. The round honors the legacy shape: with the switch on and subagents active it awaits the settles directly (`Future.wait`) instead of racing a zero-length ceiling sleep — without that, the zero deadline would have woken every round instantly and burned the 10-round cap in microseconds, detaching anyway. Doc comments updated (`HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs`, the lifecycle method, and the AGENTS.md bullet) to state the shell-scoped semantics explicitly.

**RED → GREEN:**
- Pure UTs in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`: `shellDrainDisabled` with only subagents → `drain` (even with the ceiling spent), with shell jobs → `detach` immediately, with neither → `exit`; the existing shared-ceiling cases now pin that a spent ceiling detaches subagents too when the knob is non-zero.
- New IT `shellJobDrainMs: 0 keeps the legacy subagent drain — an in-flight subagent still drains before exit` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — a background `task` child that settles at 800 ms must still re-enter as a `<task-result` wake run before exit with `drainMs: 0`. Pre-fix the run detached immediately and the result was lost; now it drains and exits 0 with no detach line. The existing shell-job `0` kill-switch IT still passes (shell jobs detach at once).

# Rework: gh-1459 — address the 4 open review threads on the headless drain

## Issues/Notes

- **Review state at leg start**: decision NONE with **4 open suggestion threads** on
  `agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` / `headless_config.dart` (all SUGGESTION level — the
  automated legs APPROVE with 0 blocking / 0 important). CI reported **no failed
  checks**. Each thread got a code fix with a RED→GREEN test per the TDD rules:
  1. A late drain wake consumed every crossed quiet bucket with ONE steer.
  2. `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disabled the pre-existing (pre-gh-1459) subagent drain.
  3. The detach line attributed the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain.
  4. The unclamped elapsed `Duration` could reach the notice text (negative clause under the fake-clock seam).
- The two remaining "open threads" in `pr_discussions_raw.json` are **top-level PR
  comments, not review threads** — they carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so there
  is nothing to reply to in-thread: the "Automated Code Review — APPROVE" summary only
  points at the 4 inline threads (replied below), and the verdict record explicitly
  says "Do not edit or reply".
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) remain untouched; under a non-zero
  ceiling both drain legs still share it per ticket.

## Approach

TDD, RED → GREEN → targeted suites → full suite (background, frozen tree):

1. **Late-wake liveness burst (thread 1)** — implemented the reviewer's first option
   (per-bucket steering) so the ticket invariant "N crossings ⇒ exactly N notices"
   holds unconditionally: `_steerHeadlessLiveness` steers one notice per
   newly-crossed bucket, each stamped from its own threshold via the extracted
   `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice`. A model probe still suppresses the whole burst
   (consumed, never re-steered) — documented at the consumption point.
2. **`shellJobDrainMs: 0` scope (thread 2)** — implemented the first option (behavior,
   not just docs): the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` now takes
   `hasActiveSubAgents`/`hasActiveShellJobs` + `shellDrainDisabled`; with `0`, live
   shell jobs detach immediately while in-flight subagents keep the legacy
   unconditional drain. `_headlessDrainRound` awaits subagent settles directly in
   that mode (a zero deadline would otherwise wake every round instantly and burn
   the round cap without waiting). Doc comments + the AGENTS.md bullet now state the
   shell-scoped semantics.
3. **Detach-line attribution (thread 3)** — threaded the loop-exit reason: a new pure
   `headlessDrainDetachCause(drainMs, roundCapEnded)` prints
   `drain ceiling (N ms)` or `round cap (10 rounds)` — the real lever, not a
   both-causes hedge.
4. **Elapsed clamp (thread 4)** — belt and suspenders: the notice text is now built
   from the per-bucket threshold duration (structurally non-negative), and
   `headlessLivenessElapsedText` additionally clamps negative inputs to `0s`.
5. **Complexity hygiene** — the per-bucket loop pushed `_steerHeadlessLiveness` to
   complexity 11 (gate: 12); extracted the notice builder, back to max 9
   (`crap4dart analyze` clean on the touched files).

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction` split into
  subagent/shell legs + `shellDrainDisabled`; new pure `headlessDrainDetachCause`;
  `headlessLivenessElapsedText` clamps negatives; `shellJobDrainMs` doc states the
  shell-scoped kill switch.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` — `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` threads
  `shellDrainDisabled` + `roundCapEnded`; `_headlessDrainRound` has the legacy
  unconditional subagent-wait leg; `_finishHeadlessDrain` names the real cause;
  `_steerHeadlessLiveness` steers per crossed bucket via
  `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice`.
- `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` — drain-decision group rewritten for the new
  signature (+ disabled-mode cases), detach-cause group, negative-elapsed clamp test.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_liveness_test.dart` — `advanceClockBy` harness
  support + the late-wake burst IT (3 crossed buckets ⇒ exactly 3 notices).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — `_ChainedRouter` + the
  10-round-cap detach-attribution IT; `_SubagentDrainRouter` + the
  subagent-drains-with-`shellJobDrainMs: 0` IT.
- `AGENTS.md` — the drain bullet states the shell-scoped `0` kill switch.

## Test Coverage

- `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` — 23/23 green (defaults, strict parse, `0`
  kill switches, round-trip, the drain decision incl. all disabled-mode cases, the
  detach-cause clauses, the liveness decision, the elapsed text incl. the clamp).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_liveness_test.dart` — 3/3 green (5m/10m
  cadence, probe suppression, and the new late-wake burst IT — failed pre-fix with
  1 collapsed notice).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — 7/7 green (mid-drain
  settle, error settle, suppressed job, ceiling detach, `shellJobDrainMs: 0`
  shell-job kill switch, the new round-cap attribution IT, and the new
  subagent-drains-with-`0` IT — failed pre-fix, the result was detached).
- Regression suites re-run green: `stuck_tool_session_test` (asserts the
  `drain ceiling` wording — unchanged for the ceiling cause), `bash_job_resolution`,
  `shell_jobs`, `shell_jobs_isolation`, `cli_config`, both parity suites — 261/261.
- `dart analyze` clean on the touched files; `crap4dart analyze` max complexity 9
  (threshold 12).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: background job
  `sh-40-hn2zh2r6ea54hyja` on the frozen tree — result appended below.

{"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. {"content":"# Rework: gh-1459 — address the 4 open review threads on the headless drain

## Issues/Notes

- **Review state at leg start**: decision NONE with **4 open suggestion threads** on
  `agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` / `headless_config.dart` (all SUGGESTION level — the
  automated legs APPROVE with 0 blocking / 0 important). CI reported **no failed
  checks**. Each thread got a code fix with a RED→GREEN test per the TDD rules:
  1. A late drain wake consumed every crossed quiet bucket with ONE steer.
  2. `shellJobDrainMs: 0` also disabled the pre-existing (pre-gh-1459) subagent drain.
  3. The detach line attributed the exit to the ceiling even when the 10-round cap ended the drain.
  4. The unclamped elapsed `Duration` could reach the notice text (negative clause under the fake-clock seam).
- The two remaining "open threads" in `pr_discussions_raw.json` are **top-level PR
  comments, not review threads** — they carry no `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so there
  is nothing to reply to in-thread: the "Automated Code Review — APPROVE" summary only
  points at the 4 inline threads (replied below), and the verdict record explicitly
  says "Do not edit or reply".
- `--wait-for-jobs` and the boot sweep (#517) remain untouched; under a non-zero
  ceiling both drain legs still share it per ticket.

## Approach

TDD, RED → GREEN → targeted suites → full suite (background, frozen tree):

1. **Late-wake liveness burst (thread 1)** — implemented the reviewer's first option
   (per-bucket steering) so the ticket invariant "N crossings ⇒ exactly N notices"
   holds unconditionally: `_steerHeadlessLiveness` steers one notice per
   newly-crossed bucket, each stamped from its own threshold via the extracted
   `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice`. A model probe still suppresses the whole burst
   (consumed, never re-steered) — documented at the consumption point.
2. **`shellJobDrainMs: 0` scope (thread 2)** — implemented the first option (behavior,
   not just docs): the pure `headlessJobDrainAction` now takes
   `hasActiveSubAgents`/`hasActiveShellJobs` + `shellDrainDisabled`; with `0`, live
   shell jobs detach immediately while in-flight subagents keep the legacy
   unconditional drain. `_headlessDrainRound` awaits subagent settles directly in
   that mode (a zero deadline would otherwise wake every round instantly and burn
   the round cap without waiting). Doc comments + the AGENTS.md bullet now state the
   shell-scoped semantics.
3. **Detach-line attribution (thread 3)** — threaded the loop-exit reason: a new pure
   `headlessDrainDetachCause(drainMs, roundCapEnded)` prints
   `drain ceiling (N ms)` or `round cap (10 rounds)` — the real lever, not a
   both-causes hedge.
4. **Elapsed clamp (thread 4)** — belt and suspenders: the notice text is now built
   from the per-bucket threshold duration (structurally non-negative), and
   `headlessLivenessElapsedText` additionally clamps negative inputs to `0s`.
5. **Complexity hygiene** — the per-bucket loop pushed `_steerHeadlessLiveness` to
   complexity 11 (gate: 12); extracted the notice builder, back to max 9
   (`crap4dart analyze` clean on the touched files).

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction` split into
  subagent/shell legs + `shellDrainDisabled`; new pure `headlessDrainDetachCause`;
  `headlessLivenessElapsedText` clamps negatives; `shellJobDrainMs` doc states the
  shell-scoped kill switch.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` — `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` threads
  `shellDrainDisabled` + `roundCapEnded`; `_headlessDrainRound` has the legacy
  unconditional subagent-wait leg; `_finishHeadlessDrain` names the real cause;
  `_steerHeadlessLiveness` steers per crossed bucket via
  `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice`.
- `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` — drain-decision group rewritten for the new
  signature (+ disabled-mode cases), detach-cause group, negative-elapsed clamp test.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_liveness_test.dart` — `advanceClockBy` harness
  support + the late-wake burst IT (3 crossed buckets ⇒ exactly 3 notices).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — `_ChainedRouter` + the
  10-round-cap detach-attribution IT; `_SubagentDrainRouter` + the
  subagent-drains-with-`shellJobDrainMs: 0` IT.
- `AGENTS.md` — the drain bullet states the shell-scoped `0` kill switch.

## Test Coverage

- `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart` — 23/23 green (defaults, strict parse, `0`
  kill switches, round-trip, the drain decision incl. all disabled-mode cases, the
  detach-cause clauses, the liveness decision, the elapsed text incl. the clamp).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_liveness_test.dart` — 3/3 green (5m/10m
  cadence, probe suppression, and the new late-wake burst IT — failed pre-fix with
  1 collapsed notice).
- `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — 7/7 green (mid-drain
  settle, error settle, suppressed job, ceiling detach, `shellJobDrainMs: 0`
  shell-job kill switch, the new round-cap attribution IT, and the new
  subagent-drains-with-`0` IT — failed pre-fix, the result was detached).
- Regression suites re-run green: `stuck_tool_session_test` (asserts the
  `drain ceiling` wording — unchanged for the ceiling cause), `bash_job_resolution`,
  `shell_jobs`, `shell_jobs_isolation`, `cli_config`, both parity suites — 261/261.
- `dart analyze` clean on the touched files; `crap4dart analyze` max complexity 9
  (threshold 12).
- Full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: background job
  `sh-40-hn2zh2r6ea54hyja` on the frozen tree — result appended below.

{"content":"## Fixed — one notice per newly-crossed bucket

Implemented the per-bucket option so the ticket's invariant ("N quiet crossings ⇒ exactly N notices") now holds unconditionally, including on a late wake.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart` — `_steerHeadlessLiveness`:** a due steer no longer consumes the *current* bucket in one shot. The code computes `currentBucket` vs `lastConsumedBucket` and, when a long reaction run left several thresholds crossed at once, steers **one notice per newly-crossed bucket** (`for (var bucket = lastBucket + 1; bucket <= currentBucket; bucket++)`), each stamped from its *own* threshold via the extracted `_steerHeadlessLivenessNotice(job, noticeElapsed: Duration(milliseconds: bucket * quietMs), tail: tail)` — so a burst after a 10-minute reaction run renders `5m`, `10m`, `15m` … rather than one collapsed notice. Probe semantics are unchanged in spirit: a `bash_job status/output` probe since the last consumption suppresses the whole burst (it was watching, not blind) but still consumes every crossed bucket — no replay on the next wake. The behavior is documented in the code comment at the consumption point, as suggested.

**RED → GREEN:** new fake-clock IT `a late drain wake (a long reaction run) steers ONE notice PER newly-crossed quiet bucket` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_liveness_test.dart` — the harness gained `advanceClockBy` to simulate a wake landing ~15m out with buckets 1–3 un-consumed; it asserts exactly 3 notice user-messages (`5m`/`10m`/`15m elapsed`) in the transcript. It failed pre-fix (1 collapsed notice) and passes now; the two pre-existing cadence/probe ITs stay green (normal wakes still land exactly one bucket at a time, so no behavior change on the tested path).

{"content":"## Fixed — the `0` kill switch is now shell-job-scoped

Took the first option: `shellJobDrainMs: 0` gates only the shell-job leg; the pre-gh-1459 subagent drain stays unconditional, so a subagent-only wait is never cut short by `0` (the knob no longer detaches more than the predecessor did).

**`lib/src/cli/headless_config.dart` — `headlessJobDrainAction`:** the pure decision now takes `hasActiveSubAgents` / `hasActiveShellJobs` (replacing the combined `hasActiveJobs`) plus `shellDrainDisabled`. With the kill switch on: a live shell job → `detach` immediately; in-flight subagents only → `drain` (legacy), regardless of the deadline. Under the default 30 min the shared ceiling still governs both loops, exactly per ticket.

**`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart`:** `_awaitHeadlessBackgroundJobs` computes `shellDrainDisabled = drainMs == 0` once and threads it through `_headlessDrainAction` and `_headlessDrainRound`. The round honors the legacy shape: with the switch on and subagents active it awaits the settles directly (`Future.wait`) instead of racing a zero-length ceiling sleep — without that, the zero deadline would have woken every round instantly and burned the 10-round cap in microseconds, detaching anyway. Doc comments updated (`HeadlessConfig.shellJobDrainMs`, the lifecycle method, and the AGENTS.md bullet) to state the shell-scoped semantics explicitly.

**RED → GREEN:**
- Pure UTs in `test/cli/headless_config_test.dart`: `shellDrainDisabled` with only subagents → `drain` (even with the ceiling spent), with shell jobs → `detach` immediately, with neither → `exit`; the existing shared-ceiling cases now pin that a spent ceiling detaches subagents too when the knob is non-zero.
- New IT `shellJobDrainMs: 0 keeps the legacy subagent drain — an in-flight subagent still drains before exit` in `test/cli/agent_cli_headless_shell_job_drain_test.dart` — a background `task` child that settles at 800 ms must still re-enter as a `<task-result` wake run before exit with `drainMs: 0`. Pre-fix the run detached immediately and the result was lost; now it drains and exits 0 with no detach line. The existing shell-job `0` kill-switch IT still passes (shell jobs detach at once).
